source.title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS

accepted.question_text: For a group G, let ν(G) be the minimal number of colors needed to color G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic symmetric subset, where a subset A of G is symmetric if A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G. Determine the invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups. In particular, is ν(F_2) finite for the free group F_2 on two generators?

evidence.quote: 1.2. Problem (R.I.Grigorchuk). Investigate the invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups. In particular, is ν(F2) finite, where F2 is the free group with two generators?

accepted.question_text: Given any finite coloring of an infinite group G, must there always exist, for every positive integer n, a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G with at least n elements?

evidence.quote: 1.6. Problem (I.Protasov). Does for every finite coloring of an infinite group G there exist a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of arbitrary big finite size?

accepted.question_text: Let ms(G, r) denote the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of a finite group G. Is it true that ms(G, r) > 1/r^2 for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1?

evidence.quote: 4.3. Question. Is ms(G, r) > 1/r^2 for every group G of odd order and every r > 1?

accepted.question_text: For every ε > 0 and every integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G such that ms(G, r) < ε, where ms(G, r) is the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset that every r-coloring of G must contain?
accepted.context_brief: Small ms values for finite groups

evidence.quote: 4.4. Question ([4]). Does for every ε > 0 and r > 1 there exist a finite group G with ms(G, r) < ε?

accepted.question_text: For a compact topological group G with Haar probability measure, let ms(G, r) be the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that every measurable r-coloring of G contains a measurable monochromatic symmetric subset of measure at least ε. Does there exist a connected compact group G and an integer r such that ms(G, r) < 1/r^2? In particular, what is the exact value of ms(SO(3), 2)?

evidence.quote: 5.4. Question ([5]). Is there a connected compact group G with ms(G, r) < 1/r^2 for some r ∈ N? In particular, what is ms(SO(3), 2) equal to?

accepted.question_text: Let S^n be the n-dimensional sphere with its invariant probability measure, and let I_2^+ be the set of orientation-preserving involutive isometries of S^n. Is ms(S^n, I_2^+, r) = 1/r^2 for all integers n, r > 1? Equivalently, does every measurable r-coloring of S^n contain a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere?

evidence.quote: 6.3. Question. Is ms(S^n, I^+_2, r) = 1/r^2 for n, r > 1? More precisely, does for every measurable r-coloring of the n-dimensional sphere S^n there exist a monochromatic subset of measure ≥ 1/r^2, symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere?

accepted.question_text: Classify the invariant ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n when n > 2. In particular, determine ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in R^n for n > 2, and compute ms(T, 2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3.

evidence.quote: 7.4. Problem. Classify ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in Rn, where n > 2. In particular, calculate ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in Rn for n > 2. Calculate ms(T, 2) (or equivalently, ms(S4 ×I, 2)) for the regular tetrahedron T in R3.

accepted.question_text: For the discrete interval [n] = {1, ..., n} and an r-coloring, let bms([n], r) be the blurred analogue of the maximal normalized size of a monochromatic symmetric subset. Calculate the values bms([n], r), at least for small n and especially when r = 2.

evidence.quote: 8.2. Problem. Calculate the values bms([n], r) (at least for small n and r = 2).

accepted.question_text: For measurable r-colorings of the unit interval [0, 1], calculate the invariant ms([0, 1], r), the largest ε such that every measurable r-coloring contains a monochromatic symmetric subset of Lebesgue measure at least ε. In particular, determine ms([0, 1], 2).

evidence.quote: 8.3. Problem. Calculate the value ms([0, 1], r) (at least for r = 2).

accepted.question_text: Let c be the constant from Theorem 8.1(7), namely the common value c = inf_{r∈N} ms([0, 1], r) r^2 = lim_{r→∞} ms([0, 1], r) r^2, which the paper bounds by 1/2 ≤ c < 5/6. Determine the exact value of c.

evidence.quote: (7) lim_{r→∞} ms([0, 1], r) r^2 = inf_{r∈N} ms([0, 1], r) r^2 = c for some constant 1/2 ≤ c < 5/6.
8.4. Problem. Calculate the constant c from Theorem 8.1(7).

accepted.question_text: How quickly do the sequences {ms([n], r)}_{n=1}^∞ and {bms([n], r)}_{n=1}^∞ converge to their common limit-related target ms([0, 1], r)?

evidence.quote: 8.5. Question. How quickly the sequences {ms([n], r)}^∞_{n=1} and {bms([n], r)}^∞_{n=1} converge to their limit ms([0, 1], r)?

needs_review.question_text_raw: 2.4. Problem ([2]). Calculate the numbers χ(Z^n) and investigate the structure of central sets in Z^n for n > 3.

evidence.quote: 2.4. Problem ([2]). Calculate the numbers χ(Z^n) and investigate the structure of central sets in Z^n for n > 3.
In this section given a group G we consider two questions: (1) what is the structure of central subsets of G and (2) what is the minimal size c(G) of a central set in G?
